Zinc Framework Guide

Overview

Zinc is a high-performance, Go-based API framework designed to compete with Gin, Echo, Chi, and Fiber. It focuses on simplicity, performance, and flexibility, making it ideal for building robust web applications and APIs.

Router

The router is the core component of Zinc, responsible for mapping HTTP requests to handler functions. It supports various HTTP methods, path parameters, wildcards, and route grouping.

Basic Routing

Zinc provides intuitive methods for handling different HTTP methods: 


app := zinc.New()

// Basic GET route
app.Get("/", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.Send("Hello, World!")
})

// Basic POST route
app.Post("/users", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "message": "User created",
    })
})

// PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS methods are also supported
app.Put("/users/:id", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "message": "User updated",
    })
})

Path Parameters

Zinc supports dynamic path parameters using the :param syntax: 


// Path parameters
app.Get("/users/:id", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    userID := c.Param("id")
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "message": fmt.Sprintf("User ID: %s", userID),
    })
})

// Multiple path parameters
app.Get("/users/:userID/posts/:postID", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "user": c.Param("userID"),
        "post": c.Param("postID"),
    })
})

Query Parameters

Accessing query parameters is straightforward: 


// Query parameters
app.Get("/search", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    query := c.Query("q")
    limit := c.Query("limit")
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "search": query,
        "limit":  limit,
    })
})

// Check if a query parameter exists
app.Get("/filter", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    if c.HasQuery("category") {
        // Process category filter
    }
})

Route Groups

Zinc provides powerful route grouping for organizing routes with common prefixes and middleware: 


// Create a route group
api := app.Group("/api")

// Routes within the group
api.Get("/users", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "users": []string{"matt", "steven"},
    })
})

// Nested groups
v1 := api.Group("/v1")
v1.Get("/products", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "products": []string{"product1", "product2"},
    })
})

// Groups can have their own middleware
adminAPI := app.Group("/admin")
adminAPI.Use(AuthMiddleware())
adminAPI.Get("/dashboard", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "stats": "Admin dashboard data",
    })
})

Middleware

Middleware functions can be applied at the application level, group level, or route level: 


// Application-level middleware
app.Use(LoggerMiddleware())

// Group-level middleware
api := app.Group("/api")
api.Use(AuthMiddleware())

// Route-level middleware
app.Get("/protected", AuthMiddleware(), func(c *zinc.Context) {
    c.Send("Protected content")
})

// Chained middleware
app.Get(
    "/admin",
    AuthMiddleware(),
    RoleMiddleware("admin"),
    func(c *zinc.Context) {
        c.Send("Admin area")
    },
)

// Defining middleware
func LoggerMiddleware() zinc.Middleware {
    return func(c *zinc.Context) {
        start := time.Now()
        c.Next() // Proceed to the next middleware or handler
        duration := time.Since(start)
        fmt.Printf("Request processed in %v\n", duration)
    }
}

Context

The Context object provides access to the request and response, as well as utility methods: 


app.Get("/context-demo", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    // Request information
    method := c.Method
    path := c.Request.URL.Path
    
    // Set status code
    c.Status(200)
    
    // Store values in context
    c.Set("user", "john")
    
    // Retrieve values from context
    user := c.Get("user")
    
    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "method": method,
        "path": path,
        "user": user,
    })
})

Request Body Parsing

Zinc makes it easy to parse JSON request bodies: 


app.Post("/users", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    type User struct {
        Name  string `json:"name" validate:"required"`
        Email string `json:"email" validate:"required,email"`
        Age   int    `json:"age" validate:"gte=0,lte=130"`
    }

    var user User
    if err := c.Body(&user); err != nil {
        c.Status(400).JSON(zinc.Map{
            "error": err.Error(),
        })
        return
    }
    
    // Validate the request body
    if errs := app.Validate(user); len(errs) > 0 {
        c.Status(400).JSON(zinc.Map{"errors": errs})
        return
    }
    
    c.Status(201).JSON(user)
})

Route Caching

Zinc uses an internal route cache to optimize performance for frequently accessed routes. This is handled automatically and requires no configuration.

Template Engine

Zinc includes a powerful templating system built on top of Go's html/template package, with additional features like template caching and custom functions.

Setup

Initialize and configure the template engine: 


// Initialize template engine
templateEngine := zinc.NewTemplateEngine("./templates")

// Set custom template functions
templateEngine.AddFunc("formatDate", func(t time.Time) string {
    return t.Format("2006-01-02")
})

// Optional: Change template file extension (default is .html)
templateEngine.SetExtension(".gohtml")

// Optional: Disable template caching for development
// templateEngine.DisableCache()

// Load all templates from the directory
if err := templateEngine.LoadTemplates(); err != nil {
    log.Fatal("Failed to load templates:", err)
}

// Register the engine with the app
app.SetTemplateEngine(templateEngine)

Rendering Templates

Render templates in your handlers: 


app.Get("/profile", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    // Data to pass to the template
    data := zinc.Map{
        "Name":     "John Doe",
        "Age":      30,
        "JoinDate": time.Now(),
    }
    
    // Render the template named "profile.html" in the templates directory
    if err := c.Render("profile", data); err != nil {
        c.Status(500).Send(err.Error())
    }
})

Template Example

Example of a template file profile.html: 


<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>User Profile</title>
</head>
<body>
    <h1>Profile for {{ .Name }}</h1>
    <p>Age: {{ .Age }}</p>
    <p>Joined: {{ formatDate .JoinDate }}</p>
</body>
</html>

Cron Jobs

Zinc provides a built-in cron scheduler for running scheduled tasks. The cron system is based on the robfig/cron package and supports all standard cron expressions.

Adding Jobs

Create and schedule jobs: 


// Schedule a job to run every minute
app.Cron("minute-job", "* * * * *", func() {
    fmt.Println("This runs every minute")
})

// Schedule a job to run every 30 seconds
app.Cron("thirty-seconds", "@every 30s", func() {
    fmt.Println("This runs every 30 seconds")
})

// Schedule a job to run at midnight every day
app.Cron("midnight-job", "0 0 * * *", func() {
    fmt.Println("This runs at midnight")
})

// Jobs can also return errors
app.Cron("error-handling", "@hourly", func() error {
    // Do something that might fail
    err := someFunction()
    if err != nil {
        return err // Errors will be logged
    }
    return nil
})

Cron Expressions

Zinc supports various cron expressions:

  • * * * * * - Standard cron expression (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week)
  • @yearly (or @annually) - Run once a year at midnight on January 1st
  • @monthly - Run once a month at midnight on the first day
  • @weekly - Run once a week at midnight on Sunday
  • @daily (or @midnight) - Run once a day at midnight
  • @hourly - Run once an hour at the beginning of the hour
  • @every 1h30m - Run at intervals (e.g., every 1 hour and 30 minutes)

File Uploads

Zinc provides a simple yet powerful file upload system with features like size limits, type validation, and multi-file uploads.

Setup

Configure the file upload handler: 


// Initialize file upload handler
fileUpload := zinc.NewFileUpload("uploads")

// Set maximum file size (5MB)
fileUpload.SetMaxSize(5 << 20)

// Set allowed file types
fileUpload.SetAllowedTypes([]string{".jpg", ".png", ".pdf"})

// Register with the app
app.SetFileUpload(fileUpload)

Single File Upload

Handle a single file upload: 


app.Post("/upload", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    // Get the uploaded file from the "file" form field
    file, err := c.File("file")
    if err != nil {
        c.Status(400).JSON(zinc.Map{"error": err.Error()})
        return
    }

    // Save the file
    filename, err := c.SaveFile(file)
    if err != nil {
        c.Status(500).JSON(zinc.Map{"error": err.Error()})
        return
    }

    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "message": "File uploaded successfully",
        "filename": filename,
    })
})

Multiple File Upload

Handle multiple file uploads: 


app.Post("/upload/multiple", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    // Get multiple uploaded files from the "files" form field
    files, err := c.Files("files")
    if err != nil {
        c.Status(400).JSON(zinc.Map{"error": err.Error()})
        return
    }

    var uploaded []string
    for _, file := range files {
        filename, err := c.SaveFile(file)
        if err != nil {
            c.Status(500).JSON(zinc.Map{"error": err.Error()})
            return
        }
        uploaded = append(uploaded, filename)
    }

    c.JSON(zinc.Map{
        "message": "Files uploaded successfully",
        "files": uploaded,
    })
})

HTML Form Example

Example HTML form for file uploads: 


<!-- Single file upload form -->
<form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
    <input type="file" name="file">
    <button type="submit">Upload File</button>
</form>

<!-- Multiple file upload form -->
<form action="/upload/multiple" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
    <input type="file" name="files" multiple>
    <button type="submit">Upload Files</button>
</form>

WebSockets

Zinc includes built-in WebSocket support for real-time communication, with features like rooms, broadcasting, and connection management.

Setup

Initialize and configure the WebSocket handler: 


// Initialize WebSocket handler
app.SetWebSocketHandler(zinc.WebSocket())

Basic WebSocket Endpoint

Create a WebSocket endpoint: 


app.Get("/ws", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    // Upgrade HTTP connection to WebSocket
    conn, err := c.Upgrade()
    if err != nil {
        c.Status(400).Send(err.Error())
        return
    }

    // Handle messages in a loop
    for {
        // Read message from WebSocket
        messageType, message, err := conn.ReadMessage()
        if err != nil {
            break // Connection closed or error occurred
        }

        // Echo the message back
        if err := conn.WriteMessage(messageType, message); err != nil {
            break
        }
    }
})

WebSocket Rooms

Implement chat rooms with WebSockets: 


app.Get("/ws/chat/:room", func(c *zinc.Context) {
    roomID := c.Param("room")

    // Upgrade HTTP connection to WebSocket
    conn, err := c.Upgrade()
    if err != nil {
        c.Status(400).Send(err.Error())
        return
    }

    // Join the room
    c.JoinRoom(roomID, conn)
    defer c.LeaveRoom(roomID, conn)

    for {
        // Read message from WebSocket
        _, message, err := conn.ReadMessage()
        if err != nil {
            break // Connection closed or error occurred
        }

        // Broadcast the message to all clients in the room
        if err := c.BroadcastToRoom(roomID, message); err != nil {
            break
        }
    }
})

Client-Side Example

Example JavaScript for connecting to the WebSocket: 


// Connect to WebSocket
const socket = new WebSocket(`ws://${window.location.host}/ws/chat/room1`);

// Connection opened
socket.addEventListener('open', (event) => {
    console.log('Connected to WebSocket');
    
    // Send a message
    socket.send(JSON.stringify({
        type: 'message',
        content: 'Hello, WebSocket!',
        sender: 'User123'
    }));
});

// Listen for messages
socket.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
    const message = JSON.parse(event.data);
    console.log('Message from server:', message);
    
    // Display the message in the UI
    displayMessage(message);
});

// Connection closed
socket.addEventListener('close', (event) => {
    console.log('WebSocket connection closed');
});

// Handle errors
socket.addEventListener('error', (event) => {
    console.error('WebSocket error:', event);
});
